Hand Hygiene

Hand hygiene — when to do it, soap vs alcohol rub, correct technique and the WHO 5 moments.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • State the WHO 5 moments of hand hygiene
  • Describe correct handwashing and hand-rub technique
  • Explain when to use soap and water vs alcohol rub

In simple words

Hand hygiene is cleaning hands to remove germs. It is the single most effective way to prevent healthcare-associated infections. Nurses perform it before and after every patient contact.

There are two methods: handwashing with soap and water, and handrubbing with alcohol-based rub.

WHO 5 moments of hand hygiene

Moment When to do it
1 Before touching a patient
2 Before a clean/aseptic procedure
3 After body fluid exposure risk
4 After touching a patient
5 After touching patient surroundings

Soap and water vs alcohol rub

Method When to use
Soap and water Hands visibly dirty, after caring for C. difficile or norovirus, before eating, after toilet
Alcohol-based rub Hands not visibly dirty, most routine clinical moments

Correct technique

  • Apply product to cover all surfaces.
  • Rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, backs of fingers, thumbs, fingertips, wrists.
  • Rub for 20–30 seconds (rub) or 40–60 seconds (wash).
  • Dry with disposable towel; use towel to turn off tap.

🔴 Hand hygiene is #1

Hand hygiene is the single most effective way to prevent infection. Perform it at all 5 WHO moments.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Before and after every patient contact — even if you wore gloves.
  • Before aseptic procedures — inserting IVs, wound dressing, catheter care.
  • After body fluids — after emptying catheters, wound care, handling specimens.
  • After patient surroundings — after touching bed rails, charts, equipment.
  • After glove removal — always clean hands after removing gloves.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Hand hygiene is the single most effective way to prevent healthcare-associated infections.
  2. WHO 5 moments: before patient contact, before clean/aseptic procedure, after body fluid exposure risk, after patient contact, after patient surroundings.
  3. Use soap and water when hands are visibly dirty or after C. difficile/norovirus.
  4. Use alcohol-based rub when hands are not visibly dirty.
  5. Clean hands after removing gloves.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Rub for 20–30 seconds; wash with soap and water for 40–60 seconds.
  2. Cover all surfaces: palms, backs, between fingers, thumbs, fingertips, wrists.
  3. Use disposable towels to dry and turn off taps.
  4. Short, clean nails; no artificial nails or nail polish for clinical staff.

📌 Memory trick

5 moments: “T-B-A-A-A” — Before Touch, Before clean procedure, After body fluids, After patient contact, After patient surroundings.

60-second revision

  • Hand hygiene = #1 infection prevention.
  • 5 WHO moments: before touch, before procedure, after body fluids, after patient contact, after surroundings.
  • Soap & water = visibly dirty; alcohol rub = not visibly dirty.
  • Rub 20–30 sec; wash 40–60 sec.
  • Clean hands after glove removal.

Test yourself

Hand hygiene should be performed:

Answer: B. Hand hygiene is performed before and after every patient contact and at all 5 WHO moments.

Use soap and water when:

Answer: B. Use soap and water when hands are visibly dirty or after C. difficile/norovirus.

Alcohol-based hand rub is used when:

Answer: B. Alcohol rub is for hands that are not visibly soiled.

Handrubbing should take:

Answer: B. Rub hands with alcohol-based rub for 20–30 seconds covering all surfaces.

Clean hands after:

Answer: B. Always clean hands after removing gloves — gloves can have micro-tears or contaminate hands during removal.
